title: Internationalization in Flutter: A Practical Approach with ARB Files
excerpt: Learn how to set up ARB files, handle pluralization, and integrate localization into your Flutter app.

content.text: In a world where users span continents, ignoring localization is a missed opportunity. Even a small app can benefit from supporting multiple languages, and Flutter provides a clean, built‑in mechanism through ARB files.

An ARB file is a JSON document with a specific set of keys. The file name follows the pattern app_en.arb for English, app_es.arb for Spanish, and so on. Inside, each entry maps a placeholder name to its translated string, optionally including placeholders for dynamic values.

Pluralization is where many developers stumble. Flutter's ARB format supports ICU message syntax, allowing you to define different forms for zero, one, many, and other quantities. For example, {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}.

In main.dart, you must register a LocalizationDelegate that loads the appropriate ARB file based on the device locale. The default AppLocalizations delegate handles this automatically, but you can customize it to load translations from a remote source if needed.
The key to maintainable i18n is to keep translations separate from UI code.

content.text: By following these patterns, you can build a Flutter app that feels native to speakers of any language, without sacrificing code clarity or performance.
